track below it.

audio_format.description: Microphone file format (the dock defaults to flac).

hide_zenvi.description: Screen: hide the Zenvi window while recording a window or region.

mic_device.description: Microphone by name (the dock's Input list); empty = keep.

preview.description: Play the timeline while recording: off, full, half or quarter resolution (always off when recording the screen).

recording_view.description: Also switch the editor to the Recording View layout (View > Recording View).

screen.description: Which screen to capture, by its name in the dock's Screen list; empty = keep.

screen_fps.description: Screen capture frame rate: 15, 24, 30 or 60 (0 = keep).

screen_region.description: Capture only this area of the screen (Region mode): {x, y, width, height} in screen pixels. Omit for the full screen.

sources.description: What to record: mic (voice), screen, webcam; any combination. Empty = keep the dock's current choice.

start_seconds.description: Timeline seconds where the recording will be placed (also moves the playhead there). Omit = wherever the playhead is when Record is pressed.

system_audio.description: Screen: also record the computer's sound output.

timeline_clip_id.description: Record over this clip, like its menu's Audio > Record: starts at the clip, on the nearest free unlocked track below it (track/start_seconds override).

track.description: Track for the recording: UI track number (1 = bottom), name or layer number; extra sources go on the tracks below it. 'none' = add to Project Files only. Empty = keep.

webcam_layout.description: Where the webcam sits over a screen recording.

webcam_resolution.description: Webcam resolution such as '1280x720' (from the dock's list); empty = keep.

webcam_size.description: Webcam corner size over a screen recording: 0.2, 0.3 or 0.4 of the frame (0 = keep).

tools.label: Prepare recording
tools.name: prepare_recording_tool

tools.description:
Run an analysis effect on a video clip, off the GUI thread, and add the result as an effect:
"stabilize the shaky shot" (Stabilizer), "track the ball / the car" (Tracker with a region box),
"detect people" (ObjectDetection, YOLO), "cut out the person / mask the dog" (ObjectMask with points
or a box). Takes seconds to minutes (about real time for Stabilizer); changes nothing on failure
or timeout; one undo step.

The result's tracked objects (Tracker/ObjectDetection/ObjectMask) can drive other effects: add Blur
or Pixelate with properties {"mask_source_id": "<effect_id>"} to blur only the tracked object
("blur the face / licence plate"), plus "mask_invert": 1 to blur everything else ("blur the
background"). Use analyze_frame_colors_tool(save_frame_path=...) to look at a frame before picking
a region. Model files are downloaded only with download_model=true. Refused: still images,
audio-only clips, locked tracks, a missing region/points, builds without OpenCV.
Example: effect="Tracker", region={"x":0.42,"y":0.30,"width":0.12,"height":0.20}, region_time=3.0.

class_filter.description: ObjectDetection: only show these labels, comma separated ('person,car').

clip_query.description: Describe the clip instead of an id: its file name or what it shows (e.g. 'beach sunset'). Add track when several clips match. Prefer timeline_clip_id.

download_model.description: Download the model files if missing (Object Detector ~10-90 MB, Object Mask ~175 MB, from the OpenShot model releases, sha256-verified).

effect.description: Stabilizer = remove camera shake; Tracker = follow a boxed object; ObjectDetection = find people/cars/animals... (YOLO); ObjectMask = cut out an object you point at.

if_exists.description: If the clip already has this effect: auto = replace a Stabilizer/Object Detector, add another Tracker/Object Mask; update = replace; add = keep both.

interpolation.description: Default interpolation for keyframes that do not name one.

mask_quality.description: ObjectMask Cutie tracking quality ('' = recommended medium).

model.description: ObjectDetection model ('' = recommended YOLO26 Nano; yoloe-* know more labels).

negative_points.description: ObjectMask: points NOT on the object (background).

properties.description: Effect properties to set, as {name: value}. A value is a number, true/false, a choice name ("HSV/HSL hue"), a color ("#00ff00") or text; or keyframes [{"time": 2.0, "value": 10, "interpolation": "linear"}] in timeline seconds to animate it. list_effects_tool(effect=...) lists every property with its range, default and choices.

region.description: Tracker: box around the object at region_time, {"x", "y", "width", "height"} as fractions of the frame (0,0 = top-left).

region_time.description: Tracker/ObjectMask: timeline seconds of the frame the region/points refer to (default: the clip's first frame).

smoothing.description: Stabilizer: frames averaged, 1-100 (30 default; higher = steadier, more crop).

timeline_clip_id.description: Timeline clip id from list_clips_tool / get_timeline_state_tool. Preferred.

timeout_seconds.description: Give up (changing nothing) after this long.

track.description: Narrow clip_query to a track: UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, or layer number.

tracker_type.description: Tracker algorithm: KCF fast (default), CSRT most accurate, MOSSE fastest.

tools.label: Stabilize / track / detect
tools.name: process_clip_effect_tool

tools.description:
Remove captions (Caption effects) from clips. It never deletes clips.

Use for "remove the captions / subtitles". Target one caption track by effect_id,
the captions of one clip by timeline_clip_id / clip_query, or all_captions=true.
The clips themselves stay; a transparent 'Captions' overlay clip that carried them
stays too (delete it with delete_from_timeline_tool if the user wants it gone).
One undo step brings the captions back.

all_captions.description: Remove every caption track in the project.

clip_query.description: Describe the captioned clip instead of an id.

timeline_clip_id.description: Remove the captions of this clip.

tools.label: Remove captions
tools.name: remove_captions_tool

tools.description:
Remove effects from clips (effect badge > Remove Effect). It never deletes timeline clips; to
delete clips use delete_from_timeline_tool. Target effect ids, or an effect name on clip(s)
("remove the blur", "take the green screen key off"), or all_effects=true to strip every effect.
For Look presets you can also use apply_look_preset_tool(look="reset_look"). One undo step.

all_effects.description: Remove every effect from the target clip(s).

clip_query.description: Describe the clip instead of an id: its file name or what it shows (e.g. 'beach sunset'). Add track when several clips match. Prefer timeline_clip_id.

effect.description: Instead of ids: remove this effect (Blur, ChromaKey...) from the target clip(s).

effect_ids.description: Effect ids to remove (get_clip_effects_tool lists them).

scope.description: Instead of ids/query: 'selected' = timeline selection, 'track' = every clip on `track`, 'all' = every clip. Clips that cannot take the effect (locked track, no picture/sound) are skipped and listed.

timeline_clip_id.description: Timeline clip id from list_clips_tool / get_timeline_state_tool. Preferred.

timeline_clip_ids.description: Several timeline clip ids to change in one step.

track.description: Narrow clip_query to a track: UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, or layer number.

tools.label: Remove effect
tools.name: remove_effect_tool

tools.description:
Remove files from Project Files (Remove from Project). The media on disk is never deleted.

Use for "remove unused files" (scope="unused": safe, no clip is touched), "clean up the
missing files" (scope="missing"), or "remove intro.mp4 from the project". A file that is
used on the timeline takes its timeline clips with it, so the call is refused until
confirm_remove_clips=true; confirm with the user first. Refused when such a clip sits on
a locked track. Cancels the file's AI generation and optimize jobs. One undo step
restores the files and their clips. To delete clips but keep the file use
delete_from_timeline_tool; this tool never deletes clips of other files.

confirm_remove_clips.description: Required when a chosen file is used on the timeline: its timeline clips are removed with it. Ask the user first.

file_ids.description: Project file ids (file_id / media_bin_file_id from list_project_files_tool).

file_query.description: Name one file instead of ids: its name, file name or a tag ('intro.mp4', 'the drone shot').

scope.description: Instead of ids/query: 'unused' = every file no timeline clip uses, 'missing' = every file whose media is gone from disk.

tools.label: Remove files from project
tools.name: remove_files_from_project_tool

tools.description:
Close empty space on a track by sliding the later clips and transitions left. Never deletes
timeline clips.

Use for "remove the gaps", "close the gap between the clips", "pack track 1 together", and
to finish a ripple delete: delete_from_timeline_tool removes a clip and leaves a hole, then
remove_gaps_tool(track=<its track>, from_seconds=<where it started>, only_first=true) closes
exactly that hole. Clips that overlap (crossfades) move together, like Track menu > Remove
All Gaps. Other tracks are not touched, so music or voice-over on another track stays where
it is. Returns the gaps closed. One undo step; nothing to close is not an error.

from_seconds.description: Only close gaps that end after this timeline time (0 = the whole track, including empty space before the first clip).

only_first.description: Close just the first gap at/after from_seconds (Remove Gap) instead of all of them (Remove All Gaps).

track.description: Track to close gaps on: UI track number (1 = bottom), name, or layer number. Empty = the one track that has gaps (refused when several do).

tools.label: Remove gaps
tools.name: remove_gaps_tool

tools.description:
Remove keyframes (animation points) from clip properties; never deletes clips.

Use it for "remove the zoom", "stop it moving", "delete the keyframe at
3 s", "clear all animation on these clips". Give the properties (or
["all"] = every animated property) and optionally a timeline time range;
without a range every keyframe of those properties goes. When a property
loses its last keyframe it falls back to the Properties dock default
(alpha 1, scale 1, location 0, rotation 0, shear 0, origin 0.5, volume 1),
exactly like Remove Keyframe in the Properties dock; to keep some other
fixed value use set_clip_properties_tool instead. To remove fades use
apply_clip_preset_tool(preset='fade_none'). One undo step.

Example: remove_keyframes_tool(timeline_clip_ids=["ABC123"], properties=["scale_x", "scale_y"])

clip_query.description: Describe one clip instead of ids.

end_seconds.description: Only remove keyframes at or before this timeline time (seconds).

properties.description: Properties whose keyframes to remove (keys or labels), or ["all"] for every animated property.

scope.description: Instead of ids/query: 'selected' = the timeline selection, 'track' = every clip on track, 'all' = every clip on the timeline.

start_seconds.description: Only remove keyframes at or after this timeline time (seconds).

timeline_clip_ids.description: Timeline clip ids to act on (from get_timeline_state_tool).

track.description: Track for clip_query or scope='track': UI track number (1 = bottom), name, or layer number.

tools.label: Remove keyframes
tools.name: remove_keyframes_tool

tools.description:
Remove timeline markers (Marker menu > Remove Marker). It never deletes clips, tracks or anything else.

Target one way: markers = ids or exact names (a name several markers share
is refused with their ids), at_seconds = the marker at that time (nearest
within 0.5 s), or all=true. One undo step brings them back. Example:
"remove the Drop marker" -> markers=['Drop']; "clear all markers" ->
all=true.

all.description: Remove every marker on the timeline.

at_seconds.description: Remove the marker at this timeline time (the nearest marker within half a second).

markers.description: Markers to remove, each a marker_id (from list_markers_tool) or an exact marker name.

tools.label: Remove marker
tools.name: remove_marker_tool

tools.description:
Remove a track lane from the timeline (Track menu > Remove Track).

It never deletes clips unless with_clips=true: a track that still holds
clips or transitions is refused with how many it has. with_clips=true
deletes the lane together with its clips and transitions, in one undo
step (undo brings everything back). To delete the clips but keep the lane
use delete_from_timeline_tool with scope='track'. Locked tracks and the last
remaining track cannot be removed. The tracks above move down one number;
the result's `tracks` list is the new numbering. Example: "remove the empty
track" -> track='3'.

track.description: Track lane to remove: UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, track id (L3) or layer number.

with_clips.description: The track still has clips or transitions: true deletes them together with the lane (Track menu > Remove Track); false refuses, so tidying up empty lanes never deletes clips by accident.

tools.label: Remove track
tools.name: remove_track_tool

tools.description:
Remove transitions from the timeline (Transition menu > Remove Transition). Never deletes clips.

The clips stay exactly where they are: two clips that overlapped keep overlapping and
now cut at the start of the later clip. "Remove all transitions on track 2" ->
scope='track', track='2'. One undo step brings them back. Refused on locked tracks.
To delete timeline clips use delete_from_timeline_tool.

at_seconds.description: Instead of ids: the transition under this timeline time (on `track` when given).

between_clip_ids.description: Instead of ids: the two timeline clip ids the transition joins, e.g. [clip_a, clip_b].

scope.description: 'selected' = selected transitions, 'track' = every transition on `track`, 'all' = every transition on the timeline.

track.description: Track to look on (UI track number, 1 = bottom; name; or layer number). With scope='track' every transition on it.

tools.label: Remove transition
tools.name: remove_transition_tool

tools.description:
Loop a clip's playback N times within one timeline clip (Clip menu > Speed > Repeat).

Use for "loop the beat 4 times" (times=4), "boomerang this" (pattern='ping_pong', times=3),
"repeat it with a half-second pause" (delay_seconds=0.5), "loop it, speeding up each time"
(speed_ramp_percent=25). The clip becomes N times as long (plus delays); the tool refuses
to run into the next clip unless ripple=true or allow_overlap=true. A clip that is already
looped must be reset first (set_clip_speed_tool reset=true) or undone. To place separate
copies instead, use duplicate_clips_tool. One undo step.

allow_overlap.description: Let the longer clip overlap the next clip on its track (the receipt lists it). Off by default: the tool refuses and says what is in the way.

clip_query.description: Describe one clip instead of ids.

delay_seconds.description: Pause (hold the last frame) between passes.

pattern.description: loop = start over each time; ping_pong = forward, backward, forward...

ripple.description: Shift the later clips on the track by the change in length, so nothing overlaps and no gap opens.

scope.description: Instead of ids/query: 'selected' = the timeline selection, 'track' = every clip on track, 'all' = every clip on the timeline.

speed_ramp_percent.description: Each pass plays this much faster (+) or slower (-) than the one before, in percent.

timeline_clip_ids.description: Timeline clip ids to act on.

times.description: How many times the clip plays in total (2 = the clip then one repeat).

track.description: Track for clip_query or scope='track': UI track number (1 = bottom), name, or layer number.

tools.label: Repeat clip
tools.name: repeat_clip_tool

tools.description:
Clear the playback frame cache, the stored waveform data, or the undo history.

playback_cache is harmless (frames re-render). waveforms is one undo step
(waveforms are regenerated when shown again). undo_history empties undo and
redo for this session and marks the project unsaved; it needs confirm=true.
Never deletes clips or media.

confirm.description: Must be true for undo_history: it cannot be undone. Ask the user first.

target.description: playback_cache = drop cached preview frames (Ctrl+Shift+Esc; fixes stale previews); waveforms = drop stored waveform data from files and clips (Edit > Clear > Waveform); undo_history = forget every undo/redo step (Edit > Clear > History).

tools.label: Reset caches / history
tools.name: reset_caches_and_history_tool

tools.description:
Replace the project file with one of its recovery copies and reopen it (File > Recovery).

The current project file is kept first as '<name>-<time>-backup.zvn' next to
it, so nothing is lost. Refuses while there are unsaved changes unless
discard_unsaved=true. Undo history becomes the restored file's history.

discard_unsaved.description: Throw away unsaved changes in the open project. Only after the user agreed.

tools.label: Restore recovery version
tools.name: restore_recovery_version_tool

tools.description:
Reverse transitions (Transition menu > Reverse Transition): play the transition backwards.

Mirrors the progress and edge curves in time. Right for a fade on ONE clip edge: a
fade-in becomes a fade-out and back. On a crossfade/wipe BETWEEN two clips it makes the
later clip show first and the earlier one flash back before the cut (the receipt's
order becomes 'later_first'), which is rarely wanted: for "make the wipe go the other
way" use update_transition_tool(flip_wipe_side=true). Several transitions in one undo
step (scope='track' reverses a whole track). Refused on locked tracks; never deletes clips.

at_seconds.description: Instead of ids: the transition under this timeline time (on `track` when given).

between_clip_ids.description: Instead of ids: the two timeline clip ids the transition joins, e.g. [clip_a, clip_b].

scope.description: 'selected' = selected transitions, 'track' = every transition on `track`, 'all' = every transition on the timeline.

track.description: Track to look on (UI track number, 1 = bottom; name; or layer number). With scope='track' every transition on it.

tools.label: Reverse transition
tools.name: reverse_transition_tool

tools.description:
Save one frame of the timeline as a full-resolution image (File > Save Current Frame).

For a thumbnail or still ("save this frame", "grab a still at 12 s").
Renders at the project's full size, not the preview size. Changes nothing
in the project.

file_path.description: Output image path (.png or .jpg). Empty = the export folder, 'Frame-<n>.png'.

time.description: Timeline seconds of the frame. -1 = the playhead.

tools.label: Save frame as image
tools.name: save_frame_image_tool

tools.description:
Save the project (File > Save Project) or save it under a new path (Save Project As).

Empty file_path saves to the current file; a never-saved project needs a
file_path. Writes undo history (capped by the history-limit preference) and a
recovery copy, like the editor's own save. Refuses to overwrite another
existing file unless overwrite=true. Failures are reported as errors.

file_path.description: Where to save. Empty = the project's current file (Save). A new path = Save As (.zvn is added when there is no project extension; missing folders are created).

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file that is not this project's current file.

tools.label: Save project
tools.name: save_project_tool

tools.description:
Find emoji in the Emojis dock's 1,239 OpenMoji stickers by name, character, code or group.

The set has faces, animals, food, travel, activities, objects and symbols (no
people, hands or flags).

Use when the user wants to see options ("what fire emojis are there", "show me food
emoji") or when add_emoji_tool picked the wrong one. Each match has the emoji
character, its name, group and code (pass the code to add_emoji_tool). Read-only.

group.description: Only this emoji group (the Emojis dock's dropdown). Empty = all.

query.description: A name or word ('fire', 'heart', 'thumbs up', 'coffee'), an emoji character ('🔥') or an OpenMoji code ('1F525'). Empty lists a group.

tools.label: Search emoji
tools.name: search_emojis_tool

tools.description:
Move the playhead (go to a time, frame, marker, the start/end, or the next/previous marker or cut).

Give exactly one of: seconds (timeline seconds: "go to 1:05" -> 65), frame,
marker (a name like 'Drop' or a marker_id), or to = 'start' | 'end' |
'next_marker' | 'previous_marker' | 'next_edit' | 'previous_edit'. The
preview shows the frame there and the Properties panel follows it.
play=true starts playback from the new position. The result has the
playhead frame, seconds and timecode (HH:MM:SS,FF as on the ruler), and
whether it is playing. Examples: "jump to the drop" -> marker='Drop';
"play from the start" -> to='start', play=true; "next cut on track 1" ->
to='next_edit', track='1'.

marker.description: Go to the marker with this name or marker_id (see list_markers_tool).

play.description: Start playback from the new position (e.g. 'play from the start' = to='start', play=true).

seconds.description: Go to this timeline time in seconds (0:32 = 32, 1:05 = 65).

to.description: Go to: 'start' / 'end' of the timeline (Home / End); 'next_marker' / 'previous_marker' (the editor's Next / Previous Marker: markers, the timeline start and end, and the edges and keyframes of selected clips); 'next_edit' / 'previous_edit' (the nearest clip start or end: a cut point).

track.description: For to='next_edit' / 'previous_edit': only clip edges on this track (UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, track id (L3) or layer number).

tools.label: Move playhead
tools.name: seek_playhead_tool

tools.description:
Select clips, transitions or effects on the timeline, as clicking, Ctrl+click, Ctrl+A or Alt+A would.

The selection is what the Properties panel shows and what other tools use
for scope='selected'. Say what to select with ids, clip_query, track (every
clip on it) and/or a time range (start_seconds..end_seconds, on every track
or on `track`). mode: 'replace' (default), 'add', 'remove', 'all', 'none',
'ripple'. Returns the resulting selection. Selecting is not an undo step
and does not change the project. Examples: "select every clip on track 1"
-> track='1'; "select the clips between 0:10 and 0:20" ->
start_seconds=10, end_seconds=20; "deselect everything" -> mode='none'.

clip_query.description: Describe one clip instead of ids (file name or content, e.g. 'the interview clip'); track narrows it.

effect_ids.description: Effect ids from a clip's effects; the Properties panel then shows that effect.

include_transitions.description: With track or a time range: also select the transitions there.

mode.description: 'replace' (default) = select exactly these; 'add' / 'remove' = add them to / take them out of the current selection; 'all' = every clip and transition (Ctrl+A); 'none' = clear the selection (Ctrl+Shift+A); 'ripple' = these (or the current selection) plus everything after them on the same track (Alt+A).

show_properties.description: Also bring the Properties panel to the front, like double-clicking a clip.

start_seconds.description: Clips overlapping the range start_seconds..end_seconds (timeline seconds). Without end_seconds: clips under that moment.

timeline_clip_ids.description: Timeline clip ids (list_clips_tool / get_timeline_state_tool).

track.description: Every clip on this track (UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, track id (L3) or layer number); with start/end only the clips in that range.

tools.label: Select on timeline
tools.name: select_timeline_items_tool

tools.description:
Split a clip's sound onto its own audio-only clip and mute the original (Clip menu > Audio >
Separate Audio).

Use for "separate the audio from the talking-head clip", "detach the sound so I can move it",
"put the left and right channels on their own tracks" (per_channel=true). The new clip covers
the same time, plays only sound (video off) and goes on the track below (or to_track); the
original keeps its picture with its audio turned off. Refused for clips without audio, clips
whose audio is already off, and when the destination is locked or already has clips there
(unless allow_overlap=true). One undo step. Returns the new audio clip ids.

allow_overlap.description: Put the audio clip there even if it overlaps clips already on that track.

clip_query.description: Describe one clip instead of ids.

per_channel.description: One audio clip per channel (left/right...) on successive tracks below, instead of one clip with all channels.

scope.description: Instead of ids/query: 'selected' = the timeline selection, 'track' = every clip on track, 'all' = every clip on the timeline.

timeline_clip_ids.description: Timeline clip ids to act on.

to_track.description: Track for the new audio clip: UI track number (1 = bottom), name, or layer number. Empty = the track directly below (created when there is none), like the menu.

track.description: Track for clip_query or scope='track': UI track number (1 = bottom), name, or layer number.

tools.label: Separate audio
tools.name: separate_clip_audio_tool

tools.description:
Turn a clip's sound or picture on or off, or show/hide its waveform on the timeline.

Use for "mute this clip" (audio='off'), "unmute it" (audio='auto'), "make it audio only" /
"hide the video but keep the sound" (video='off'), "show the waveform" (waveform='show').
This switches the track of sound or picture entirely; to change how loud a clip is use
set_clip_volume_tool, and to get the sound onto its own clip use separate_clip_audio_tool.
Refused on locked tracks and for 'on'/'show' when the media has no audio/video. Already in
that state is not an error (no undo step). One undo step. Waveforms are drawn a moment later.

audio.description: Clip sound: off = mute the clip entirely, on = force on, auto = as the media has it (Properties > Enable Audio). '' = leave it.

clip_query.description: Describe one clip instead of ids.

scope.description: Instead of ids/query: 'selected' = the timeline selection, 'track' = every clip on track, 'all' = every clip on the timeline.

timeline_clip_ids.description: Timeline clip ids to act on.

track.description: Track for clip_query or scope='track': UI track number (1 = bottom), name, or layer number.

video.description: Clip picture: off = sound only (audio-only clip), on/auto = show the picture (Properties > Enable Video). '' = leave it.

waveform.description: Draw the clip's audio waveform on the timeline, or hide it.

tools.label: Clip audio/video on-off
tools.name: set_clip_audio_video_tool

tools.description:
Set one or more properties of one or more timeline clips to fixed values.

Use it for "make it 50% transparent" (alpha 0.5), "use the multiply blend
mode" (composite), "fit/fill the frame" (scale Best Fit / Crop), "pin it to the
top right" (gravity), "make it half size" (scale_x/scale_y 0.5), "move it
left" (location_x), "tilt it 10 degrees" (rotation), "mirror it"
(scale_x -1; mirrors in place only with a centred gravity, otherwise the
receipt warns), "rounded corners" (corner_radius), "turn it down" (volume),
"show frame numbers" (display). Several properties and several clips in
one call, one undo step. A static value replaces any animation of that
property (the receipt says so); to animate or change only part of a
curve use set_keyframes_tool, and for fades, zooms, slides or layouts use
apply_clip_preset_tool. Timeline position, trim and track are not
properties here (use the timeline editing tools). Clips on locked tracks
are refused (or skipped with scope).

Example: set_clip_properties_tool(timeline_clip_ids=["ABC123"],
properties={"alpha": 0.5, "composite": "multiply"})

at_seconds.description: Leave empty for static values (an animated property is flattened to the new value). Give a timeline time (seconds) to set the value only at that moment, as a keyframe, like editing in the Properties dock with the playhead there; other keyframes stay.

clip_query.description: Describe one clip instead of ids.

properties.description: Property -> value, several at once. Keys are property keys or their Properties-dock labels; values are numbers, choice names or colors. Examples: {"alpha": 0.5} (50% opacity), {"scale": "Best Fit"} (Crop | Best Fit | Stretch | None), {"gravity": "top right"}, {"composite": "multiply"} (blend mode: Normal, Darken, Multiply, Color Burn, Lighten, Screen, Color Dodge, Add, Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Difference, Exclusion), {"scale_x": 0.4, "scale_y": 0.4}, {"location_x": 0.25} (-1..1 = one frame width), {"rotation": 15} (degrees), {"scale_x": -1} (mirror; in place only with a centred gravity such as Center), {"corner_radius": 0.1, "margin": 0.04}, {"volume": 0.8} (0-1.3), {"wave_color": "#ff8800"}, {"display": "Timeline"} (frame-number overlay), {"mixing": "Average"}, {"waveform": true}.

scope.description: Instead of ids/query: 'selected' = the timeline selection, 'track' = every clip on track, 'all' = every clip on the timeline.

timeline_clip_ids.description: Timeline clip ids to act on (from get_timeline_state_tool).

track.description: Track for clip_query or scope='track': UI track number (1 = bottom), name, or layer number.

tools.label: Set clip properties
tools.name: set_clip_properties_tool

tools.description:
Speed clips up or slow them down, play them backwards, or retime them to an exact length
(Clip menu > Speed). Keyframes and the audio follow the new timing.

Use for "speed up the drone shot 2x" (speed=2), "slow motion" (speed=0.5), "play it in
reverse" (reverse=true), "make this clip exactly 3 seconds" (target_duration_seconds=3),
"back to normal speed" (speed=1, absolute=true keeps the same part of the source; reset=true
is the menu's Reset). speed combines with reverse. Speeds from 1/16x to 16x.

A slower clip gets longer and may run into the next clip on its track: the tool refuses
unless ripple=true (push later clips along) or allow_overlap=true. Looped clips
(repeat_clip_tool) need reset=true before a new speed. For a still frame use
freeze_frame_tool; to loop use repeat_clip_tool. One undo step for all clips. Returns each
clip's length before/after and its effective speed.

absolute.description: Read speed relative to the original media instead (1 = normal speed, 2 = double normal), keeping the same part of the source.

allow_overlap.description: Let the longer clip overlap the next clip on its track (the receipt lists it). Off by default: the tool refuses and says what is in the way.

clip_query.description: Describe one clip instead of ids.

reset.description: Clip > Speed > Reset first: normal speed, forward, loops removed. Like the menu, the clip then runs from its in point to the end of its source.

reverse.description: Flip the playback direction (a reversed clip plays forward again).

ripple.description: Shift the later clips on the track by the change in length, so nothing overlaps and no gap opens.

scope.description: Instead of ids/query: 'selected' = the timeline selection, 'track' = every clip on track, 'all' = every clip on the timeline.

speed.description: Speed factor relative to how the clip plays now: 2 = twice as fast (half as long), 0.5 = half speed, 1.5, 4... 0 = leave the speed alone.

target_duration_seconds.description: Retime so the clip lasts exactly this long on the timeline (speeds up or slows down as needed); 0 = unused.

timeline_clip_ids.description: Timeline clip ids to act on.

track.description: Track for clip_query or scope='track': UI track number (1 = bottom), name, or layer number.

tools.label: Change clip speed
tools.name: set_clip_speed_tool

tools.description:
Rearrange the editor window: switch view, open/close panels and scopes, toolbar, fullscreen, custom views.

Use for "switch to the color view", "show the scopes", "open the
properties panel", "go fullscreen", "save this layout as Review". Uses the
View menu's own actions. Not an undo step (layout is an editor preference).
Example: {"view": "color"}; {"show_panels": ["Histogram"], "save_view_as": "Grade"}

delete_view.description: Delete this saved custom view (by name). Never touches the project.

dock_all.description: Dock every floating panel back into the window.

save_view_as.description: After the changes, save the layout as a new custom view with this name.

scopes.description: Open or close every scope (Histogram, Luma Waveform, Vectorscope, Audio Levels).

show_panels.description: Panels to open, e.g. ['Properties', 'Effects', 'Histogram', 'Color Wheels', 'Captions'] (default none).

toolbar.description: Show or hide the main toolbar.

update_active_view.description: After the changes, overwrite the active custom view with the layout.

view.description: Switch view: 'simple' (default editing), 'color' (Properties, Color Wheels and scopes), 'recording' (Recording dock), or the name of a saved custom view.

tools.label: Change editor layout
tools.name: set_editor_layout_tool

tools.description:
Store an export default in the project (used by export_video_tool when that argument is not given).

Values are validated (unknown keys are refused with the list of valid ones)
and saved with the project, outside undo history -- like the Export
dialog remembering its fields. Prefer passing arguments to export_video_tool
directly; use this when the user wants a setting remembered.
Example: {"key": "preset", "value": "YouTube"}; {"key": "start", "clear": true}

clear.description: Remove the stored override for key (or every override when key is empty).

key.description: Setting to store: preset, quality, export_type, width, height, fps, start, end, video_codec, audio_codec, format, video_bitrate, audio_bitrate, sample_rate, channels, output_path, folder, file_name, image_format (also start_frame, end_frame, fps_num, fps_den).

value.description: New value (see get_export_settings_tool valid_keys for each key's format).

tools.label: Update export setting
tools.name: set_export_setting_tool

tools.description:
Animate one property of one timeline clip with timed keyframes.

Use it for custom motion the presets do not cover: "zoom from 100% to 130%
between 2 s and 5 s", "move the logo from left to right", "fade the music
down to 20% at 10 s", "spin it once", or any exact curve. Times are per
point: 'seconds' counts from the clip's first visible frame (so 0 is the
clip's start even when it is trimmed), 'timeline_seconds' is timeline
time, 'source_seconds' is time in the media, 'frame' is the raw keyframe
X. Every point must land inside the clip. 'value' is in the property's
units (scale 1 = 100%, location -1..1 = one frame, rotation degrees, alpha
0-1, volume 0-1.3); omit it to pin the current value at that time. Shape
each move with interpolation (bezier, linear, constant) or one of the 28
bezier ease presets. mode='replace' (default) makes these points the whole
curve; 'merge' keeps the other points; 'replace_range' clears only the span
the new points cover. For whole-clip zooms, pans, fades and slides prefer
apply_clip_preset_tool; to remove keyframes use remove_keyframes_tool.
One undo step.

Example: set_keyframes_tool(timeline_clip_id="ABC123", property="scale_x",
points=[{"seconds": 0, "value": 1}, {"seconds": 4, "value": 1.3, "ease": "ease_in_out"}])

clip_query.description: Describe the clip instead of an id: its file name or what it shows (e.g. 'beach sunset'). Add track when several clips match. Prefer timeline_clip_id.

ease.description: Default bezier ease for points that set none (e.g. 'ease_in_out').

interpolation.description: Default interpolation for points that set none ('' = bezier, constant for choice properties).

mode.description: replace = these points become the whole curve; merge = add/update these points and keep the others; replace_range = drop existing points between the first and last new point, keep the rest.

occurrence.description: With clip_query: take the Nth matching clip in timeline order (0 = best match).

points.description: Keyframes: each gives one time (frame, seconds, timeline_seconds or source_seconds) and a value. Example: [{"seconds": 0, "value": 1}, {"seconds": 3, "value": 1.3, "ease": "ease_in_out"}].

ease.description: Bezier ease preset (the Properties dock's list) for the move INTO this point; implies bezier.

frame.description: Clip frame X exactly as stored: 1-based and counting trimmed-off source frames (the first visible frame is round(start*fps)+1).

interpolation.description: How the value moves INTO this point from the previous one: bezier (smooth), linear, or constant (holds the previous value, then jumps).

seconds.description: Seconds from the clip's first visible frame: 0 = where the clip starts on the timeline, the clip's duration = its end. Works the same on trimmed clips.

source_seconds.description: Time in the source media in seconds (inside the clip's trimmed range).

timeline_seconds.description: Timeline time in seconds (must fall inside the clip).

value.description: Value at that time: a number (alpha 0-1, scale 1 = 100%, location -1..1 = one frame, rotation in degrees, volume 0-1.3, time = source frame), a choice name for choice properties (has_audio: Auto/Off/On), or a color for wave_color. Omit to keep the value the curve already has there (pins it).

position_near.description: With clip_query: prefer the clip under this timeline time (seconds).

property.description: The clip property to animate: 'scale_x', 'scale_y', 'location_x', 'location_y', 'rotation', 'alpha', 'volume', 'shear_x', 'shear_y', 'origin_x', 'origin_y', 'corner_radius', 'margin', 'wave_color', 'has_audio', 'has_video', 'channel_filter', 'channel_mapping' or 'time' (or its label, e.g. 'Scale X').

timeline_clip_id.description: Timeline clip id from list_clips_tool / get_timeline_state_tool. Preferred.

track.description: Narrow clip_query to a track: UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, or layer number.

tools.label: Animate clip property
tools.name: set_keyframes_tool

tools.description:
Change one editor preference, validated against its type and allowed values, or restore a tab's defaults.

Takes effect like the Preferences dialog (autosave timer, cache, theme,
decoder, shortcuts...); restart_required in the receipt says when a
restart is needed. Refuses unknown keys (with suggestions), out-of-range
numbers, invalid choices, conflicting shortcuts and internal or protected
settings. Not an undo step: call again with the previous value to revert.

key.description: Preference key (or its title) from get_preferences_tool, e.g. 'autosave-interval'.

restore_tab.description: Instead of key/value: restore every preference on this tab to its default (Preferences > Restore Defaults).

value.description: New value: true/false, a number within min/max, a dropdown value or name, text, or a shortcut like 'Ctrl+Shift+K' (several: 'Ctrl+K | F5').

tools.label: Change preference
tools.name: set_preference_tool

tools.description:
Change the project's video format: size, aspect and frame rate (File > Choose Profile).

Use for "make this an Instagram reel / TikTok / YouTube Short" (profile=
'instagram_reel' etc. -> 1080x1920 9:16), "square for Instagram",
"switch to 4K 24 fps" (profile='cinema_4k' or profile='4k', fps=24), "make
it vertical" (orientation='portrait'), or "match this clip" (from_file_id).
Landscape footage in a vertical project is letterboxed unless you pass
reframe='fill' (crop to fill, centred) -- do that when the user wants the
picture to fill the frame. Keyframes and trims follow a frame-rate change.
One undo step reverts the profile and the reframe. Export settings saved
in the Export dialog are reset when the profile changes.
Example: {"profile": "instagram_reel", "reframe": "fill"}

fps.description: Frame rate, e.g. 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 60. 0 = keep (or the preset's).

from_file_id.description: Match a project file's size and frame rate (media_bin_file_id from list_files_tool).

height.description: Frame height in pixels (with width). 0 = unchanged.

orientation.description: Turn the (current or named) profile to this shape: 'portrait' makes 1920x1080 -> 1080x1920.

profile.description: Profile name ('FHD Vertical 1080p 30 fps'), key ('01080x1920p0030_09-16'), social preset ('instagram_reel', 'tiktok', 'youtube_shorts', 'instagram_post', 'instagram_portrait', 'youtube', 'youtube_4k', 'cinema', '4k') or 'WIDTHxHEIGHT'. Empty = keep the current one.

reframe.description: Existing full-frame clips whose shape differs from the new frame: keep = unchanged (letterboxed/pillarboxed), fit = whole picture with bars, fill = crop to fill, centred. Titles and picture-in-picture clips are never changed.

width.description: Frame width in pixels (with height) instead of a profile name. 0 = unchanged.

tools.label: Set project format
tools.name: set_project_profile_tool

tools.description:
Change individual project settings: frame rate, frame size, audio sample rate and channels.

Video values go through the same profile switch as set_project_profile_tool
(a matching built-in profile, or a saved custom one for unusual sizes), so
keyframes follow an fps change. Audio: sample_rate / channels set the
project's mix format (used by export and the timeline); the preview may
re-sync the sample rate to the audio device, and opening a project re-applies
Preferences > Default Audio Sample Rate / Channels unless save_as_default=true.
One undo step; a call that changes nothing adds none.
Example: {"fps": 24} or {"sample_rate": 44100, "channels": "mono"}

orientation.description: Turn the frame to this shape.

preset.description: Alias of profile for social presets: 'instagram_reel', 'tiktok', 'youtube', ...

profile.description: Profile name or social preset instead of size/fps (see set_project_profile_tool).

reframe.description: What happens to existing full-frame clips of another shape (see set_project_profile_tool).

save_as_default.description: Also store sample_rate/channels as the Preferences default for new projects (takes effect after restart).

tools.label: Set project settings
tools.name: set_project_setting_tool

tools.description:
Change how the timeline is shown: zoom in/out/fit, show N seconds or a time range, center on the playhead, and turn snapping, razor or timing mode on or off.

Pick at most one zoom: zoom='in' / 'out' (steps = how many), zoom='fit'
(every clip in view), visible_seconds (e.g. 10 = ten seconds across), or
start_seconds + end_seconds (show that range). center_on_playhead scrolls
to the playhead. snapping / razor / timing switch the timeline toolbar's
modes: they only change what mouse drags and clicks do for the person
editing, not the project. Nothing here is an undo step. Examples: "zoom to
fit" -> zoom='fit'; "show me 0:30 to 1:00" -> start_seconds=30,
end_seconds=60; "turn off snapping" -> snapping=false.

center_on_playhead.description: Scroll so the playhead is in the middle (Center on Playhead).

end_seconds.description: End of the range to show (timeline seconds).

razor.description: true: clicking a clip slices it (Razor tool); false: normal clicks.

snapping.description: true: dragged clips snap to clip edges, the playhead and markers; false: free dragging.

start_seconds.description: Show exactly this range: its start (timeline seconds). Give end_seconds too.

steps.description: How many zoom steps for zoom 'in' / 'out'.

timing.description: true: dragging a clip edge retimes (speeds up / slows down) the clip instead of trimming it; false: normal trimming.

visible_seconds.description: Zoom so this many seconds fill the timeline width, centered on the playhead.

zoom.description: 'in' / 'out' = zoom one step like the = / - keys (repeat with steps); 'fit' = show every clip, from 0 to the end of the last clip.

tools.label: Timeline view
tools.name: set_timeline_view_tool

tools.description:
Cut clips at a timeline time (the Slice menu / razor tool).

Use for "split the clip at 12 seconds", "cut everything at the playhead", "cut off
everything after 30 s on track 1" (keep='left'), "drop the first part of this clip and close
the gap" (keep='right', ripple=true). Target one clip (timeline_clip_ids / clip_query), the
selection, one track, or everything under the time (scope='all'). Explicit clips must lie
under at_seconds; locked tracks are refused for explicit targets and skipped (and reported)
for scope='all'. keep='both' returns the new right-hand clip ids. One undo step.
To shorten a clip without cutting it in two, trim_clips_tool is simpler.

at_seconds.description: Timeline time to cut at; -1 = the playhead.

clip_query.description: Describe one clip to cut instead of ids.

include_transitions.description: With scope 'track'/'all'/'selected': cut transitions under the time too.

keep.description: both = cut into two clips; left = keep the part before the cut (drop the rest); right = keep the part after it.

ripple.description: With keep='left' or 'right': close the gap the dropped part leaves.

scope.description: Instead of ids/query: 'selected' = the selected clips, 'track' = everything on track under the time, 'all' = everything under the time on every unlocked track (a razor cut through the whole timeline).

timeline_clip_ids.description: Clips to cut (each must be under at_seconds).

track.description: Track for clip_query or scope='track': UI track number (1 = bottom), name, or layer number.

tools.label: Slice clips
tools.name: slice_clips_tool

tools.description:
Change where clips start and end in their source media (drag a clip edge).

Use for "trim the first two seconds", "cut the last second off every clip on track 1",
"make this clip 5 seconds long", "start the clip at 0:12 of the video". Times are seconds
of the source (source_start/source_end) or amounts to cut (trim_start_seconds /
trim_end_seconds; negative amounts extend the clip into unused source).

Trimming the start keeps the picture in place: the clip's left edge moves later and a gap
opens. With ripple=true the clip keeps its start and every later clip on the track moves to
close (or open) the room. Extending past the media, before 0 s, or over another clip is
refused with the exact limit (allow_overlap=true overlaps anyway). Still images can be any
length. To cut a clip in two use slice_clips_tool; to change speed use set_clip_speed_tool.
One undo step for the whole batch.

allow_overlap.description: Let the result overlap other clips on the track (the receipt lists what it covers). Off by default: the tool refuses and says what is in the way.

clip_query.description: Describe one clip instead of ids.

duration_seconds.description: Set the clip's length on the timeline by moving its out point; 0 = unchanged.

ripple.description: Shift the later clips on the track to follow (close/open the room), like a ripple edit. With ripple the clip keeps its start on the timeline.

scope.description: Instead of ids/query: 'selected' = the timeline selection, 'track' = every clip on track, 'all' = every clip on the timeline.

source_end.description: Set the out point: seconds into the source media; -1 = unchanged.

source_start.description: Set the in point: seconds into the source media; -1 = unchanged.

timeline_clip_ids.description: Timeline clip ids to act on.

tools.description:
Change properties of an effect that is already on a clip: static values, or keyframes to animate
them ("make the blur stronger", "fade the pixelation out over 2 seconds", "set the echo mix to 0.2").
Target one effect by effect_id, or name the effect class on one or several clips (scope='all' for
"every clip's blur"). Only the given properties change; one undo step.

Keyframes: {"sigma": [{"time": 0, "value": 8}, {"time": 2, "value": 0, "interpolation": "linear"}]}
with timeline seconds inside the clip. Colors: "#RRGGBB". Choices by name ("Basic keying").
For ColorGrade prefer color_grade_clip_tool. Refused: unknown or read-only property, out-of-range
value, locked track, a clip without that effect.

clip_query.description: Describe the clip instead of an id: its file name or what it shows (e.g. 'beach sunset'). Add track when several clips match. Prefer timeline_clip_id.

effect.description: Instead of effect_id: the effect name on the clip(s) (Blur, ColorGrade...).

effect_id.description: Effect id from get_clip_effects_tool / add_effect_tool. Preferred.

interpolation.description: Default interpolation for keyframes that do not name one.

occurrence.description: With effect: which one if a clip has several of that effect (1 = first).

properties.description: Effect properties to set, as {name: value}. A value is a number, true/false, a choice name ("HSV/HSL hue"), a color ("#00ff00") or text; or keyframes [{"time": 2.0, "value": 10, "interpolation": "linear"}] in timeline seconds to animate it. list_effects_tool(effect=...) lists every property with its range, default and choices.

scope.description: Instead of ids/query: 'selected' = timeline selection, 'track' = every clip on `track`, 'all' = every clip. Clips that cannot take the effect (locked track, no picture/sound) are skipped and listed.

timeline_clip_id.description: Timeline clip id from list_clips_tool / get_timeline_state_tool. Preferred.

timeline_clip_ids.description: Several timeline clip ids to change in one step.

track.description: Narrow clip_query to a track: UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, or layer number.

tools.description:
Rename, recolor or move an existing timeline marker.

marker is the marker_id from list_markers_tool or the marker's exact name
(a name several markers share is refused with their ids). Pass only what
should change. Example: "rename the marker at 0:32 to Chorus" -> first
list_markers_tool, then marker='<id>', name='Chorus'; "move the Drop marker
to 0:40" -> marker='Drop', position_seconds=40. One undo step.

color.description: New color tag; empty = keep. the timeline tints the marker's icon with it (blue = the default icon) and shows the marker's name next to it.

marker.description: Marker to change: its marker_id (from list_markers_tool) or its exact name.

name.description: New name. Empty string clears it. Omit to keep the name.

position_seconds.description: Move the marker to this timeline time (seconds). Omit to keep it where it is.

tools.description:
Change project files (File Properties): rename, tag, relink moved media, set in/out, set sequence fps.

Use for "rename the clip to Intro" (with rename_clips=true the timeline clips get the label
too), "tag these as b-roll" (add_tags on many file_ids at once), "I moved my footage to
~/Movies/shoot, fix the missing files" (search_folder, or path for one file), "only use
0:05-0:20 of this file" (source_start/end_seconds, source seconds), "play this image
sequence at 12 fps" (fps; image sequences only). Timeline clips that use a changed file
are refreshed (their end is clamped to the new length, as the dialog does). Relinking
keeps the name, tags, AI metadata, in/out and optimized preview, and reports
same_content=false when the new media is a different file. One undo step. Does not
trim timeline clips (that is a timeline edit) and never deletes anything.
Example: file_ids=["A1","B2"], add_tags=["b-roll"].

add_tags.description: Tags to add to every chosen file ('b-roll', 'intro').

file_ids.description: Project file ids (file_id / media_bin_file_id from list_project_files_tool).

file_query.description: Name one file instead of ids: its name, file name or a tag ('intro.mp4', 'the drone shot').

fps.description: New frame rate for IMAGE SEQUENCES only (e.g. 24, 12, 29.97); rescales its duration. 0 = keep.

path.description: Relink one file to this media path (the file moved or was replaced). For an image sequence: a frame of the new sequence or its folder. '' = keep.

remove_tags.description: Tags to remove from every chosen file.

rename_clips.description: With name: also relabel the timeline clips that use the file.

reset_in_out.description: Clear the file's in/out so it spans the whole media again.

search_folder.description: Relink every chosen file to the file with the same name found in this folder (searched recursively). '' = no search.

source_end_seconds.description: New out-point, in seconds of the source media (File Properties > End Frame). One file.

source_start_seconds.description: New in-point, in seconds of the source media (File Properties > Start Frame). One file.

tags.description: Replace the file(s) tags with exactly these. [] clears them; leave out to keep.

tools.description:
Rename a track and/or lock or unlock it (Track menu > Rename Track / Lock Track / Unlock Track).

A locked track's clips cannot be moved, trimmed, sliced, deleted or edited
until it is unlocked; renaming a locked track is fine. Pass only what should
change. Examples: "rename track 2 to B-roll" -> track='2', name='B-roll';
"lock the voiceover track" -> track='Voiceover', lock=true; "unlock
everything on track 1" -> track='1', lock=false. One undo step; asking for
the state a track already has changes nothing.

lock.description: true locks the track, false unlocks it. Omit to leave it as is.

name.description: New name for the track header. Empty string = back to the default 'Track N'. Omit to keep the current name.

track.description: Track to change: UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, track id (L3) or layer number.

tools.label: Rename or lock track
tools.name: update_track_tool

tools.description:
Change a transition on the timeline: length, position, wipe shape, softness, curves, audio crossfade.

"Make the crossfade 2 seconds" -> duration_seconds=2: on a transition between two clips
the later clip (and, with ripple=true, everything after it on that track) moves so the
clips overlap by 2 s and the transition covers the overlap; other tracks never move. On
a fade at a clip's start/end the transition keeps that edge. The progress curve is
rescaled to the new length (with the default soft edge the visible dissolve is shorter
than the transition; a lower contrast makes it more gradual). "Use a circle wipe
instead" -> mask="circle_in_to_out"; "make the wipe go the other way" ->
flip_wipe_side=true (or the mirrored mask, e.g. wipe_right_to_left); "harder edge" ->
contrast=20. Changes every chosen transition in one undo step. Refused on locked
tracks. Never deletes clips.
Example: between_clip_ids=["A","B"], duration_seconds=2.

at_seconds.description: Instead of ids: the transition under this timeline time (on `track` when given).

audio_crossfade.description: Also crossfade the two clips' audio under the transition (equal-power).

between_clip_ids.description: Instead of ids: the two timeline clip ids the transition joins, e.g. [clip_a, clip_b].

brightness_keyframes.description: Replace the progress curve (brightness): 1 = not started, -1 = finished; times from the transition start.

items.description: One keyframe of a transition curve.

seconds.description: Time from the START of the transition, 0 = its first frame.

value.description: Curve value (brightness -1..1: 1 = wipe not started, -1 = finished; contrast 0..20).

contrast.description: Edge hardness of the wipe: 0 = very soft/blurry edge, 3 = the default soft edge, 20 = a hard line.

contrast_keyframes.description: Replace the edge-hardness curve over time.

items.description: One keyframe of a transition curve.

seconds.description: Time from the START of the transition, 0 = its first frame.

value.description: Curve value (brightness -1..1: 1 = wipe not started, -1 = finished; contrast 0..20).

duration_seconds.description: New length in seconds (0 = keep). On a crossfade between two clips the later clip moves so the clips overlap by exactly this much (see keep_overlap).

flip_wipe_side.description: Wipe from the other side (left-to-right becomes right-to-left, circle-out becomes circle-in) and still go from the earlier clip to the later one. Works for any mask (inverts it and reverses its curve).

interpolation.description: Easing of the progress curve: bezier = ease in/out (default), linear = constant speed, constant = jump. '' = keep.

invert_mask.description: Raw 'mask invert' property. Alone it makes the later clip show first (it flashes back before the cut); use flip_wipe_side instead.

keep_overlap.description: With duration_seconds on a crossfade: do not move any clip (the transition may then run past the overlap and dip to the track below).

mask.description: Change the wipe shape: a transition name ('fade', 'wipe_left_to_right', 'circle_in_to_out', any list_transitions_tool name) or an image file path. '' = keep.

mask_file_id.description: Use this project image file (e.g. a gradient or logo) as the wipe shape. '' = keep.

position_seconds.description: Move the transition to start at this timeline time (clips stay).

replace_image.description: Show the mask image itself instead of transitioning (a preview aid).

ripple.description: With duration_seconds on a crossfade: move everything after the later clip on that track too, so no gap or overlap opens further down. false = move only the later clip.

scope.description: 'selected' = selected transitions, 'track' = every transition on `track`, 'all' = every transition on the timeline.

track.description: Track to look on (UI track number, 1 = bottom; name; or layer number). With scope='track' every transition on it.
